open_obligations: Check that 'a more limited class of problems' corresponds to doubly-efficient debate's need for a (potentially extensive) human-verifiable natural-language reasoning trace (LIM-HUMAN-VERIFIABLE) rather than another restriction
Read p2 L86 to p3 L7 of the citing paper, which spans a page break, to see whether it ties the more limited class of problems to debaters writing out the full human-judgeable argument
Check whether the two papers share authors; if so, the statement about doubly-efficient debate is partly self-assessment
in.other_title: Prover-estimator debate paper: doubly-efficient debate (Brown-Cohen et al.) solves a narrower class
in.rationale: The prover-estimator paper says the original debate proposal makes the too-strong assumption that both debaters are computationally unbounded, and that doubly-efficient debate (Brown-Cohen et al. [2024]) relaxes this assumption at the price of solving a more limited class of problems. The doubly-efficient debate paper states, as a key requirement and limitation for applying its results in real-world settings, that the debating models must produce natural-language reasoning traces that careful human analysis could have judged correct. Both passages name a limitation of doubly-efficient debate, but neither ties one to the other, so neither bears on the other's claim and only a shared topic is proposed; whether the more limited class of problems reflects the trace requirement is open and left to the first obligation.
in.scope: proposed SHARES_TOPIC: Limitations of doubly-efficient debate: the prover-estimator paper says it solves a more limited class of problems once it relaxes the assumption of computationally unbounded debaters, and the doubly-efficient debate paper states the requirement that the debating models produce natural-language reasoning traces that careful human analysis could judge correct; whether the two correspond is not shown; holds for theoretical work on debate protocols

text: The authors state that a key requirement and limitation for real-world use is that the debating models must be able to produce (potentially extensive) natural-language reasoning traces for the problem such that (potentially extensive) careful human analysis could have judged the reasoning correct. Given this, they say even very complex computations could be verified by querying human judgements on only a single step.
title: Limitation: needs a (possibly long) human-verifiable natural-language reasoning trace
